descriptors.descriptor_text: Host matrix capable of confining an aqueous proton-conducting phase within nanometric (1–10 nm) channels or pores to enforce interfacial-dominated transport.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Creates the high-surface-area confinement geometry necessary for the interfacial percolation network, suppressing bulk-like liquid transport in favor of surface/interfacial proton pathways.
required_material_features: pore/channel diameter in the 1–10 nm regime
high aspect ratio interconnected porosity
hydrophilic internal surfaces
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: Confinement-induced multi-threshold percolation with interfacial-dominated transport

descriptors.descriptor_text: The confined proton-conducting phase must retain a continuous, mobile hydrogen-bonded network across the full temperature range 182 K to 299 K, with no first-order freezing, eutectic phase separation, or abrupt crystallization that breaks percolation connectivity.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Ensures an uninterrupted interfacial proton pathway as the material is cooled from room temperature to sub-zero conditions, allowing the cluster-percolation network to persist across T_break and down to the cold limit.
required_material_features: suppressed bulk freezing of confined aqueous/acid phase
absence of sharp phase transitions between 182 K and 299 K
continuous hydrogen-bond connectivity across the entire temperature span
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: T_break thermodynamic connectivity shift and cold-end operability requirement (182 K)

descriptors.descriptor_text: The proton-conducting medium must incorporate a mobile acid species whose proton activity and local diffusivity remain high in the 182–273 K sub-zero window, avoiding the crystallization or glass-formation that immobilizes pure phosphoric acid near 315 K.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Provides the charge carriers for interfacial proton hopping; in H4, the acid must stay mobile and partly dissociated even after the bulk-like continuous film breaks apart into clusters, otherwise the low-temperature cluster percolation network loses its conducting units.
required_material_features: acid species with depressed freezing point (well below 273 K) when confined or complexed
sustained proton dissociation equilibrium down to 182 K
resistance to phase separation or salt precipitation on cooling
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: interfacial percolation and low-T cluster network; phosphoric acid crystallization avoidance

descriptors.descriptor_text: The interfacial region must exhibit proton-hopping activation energy in the low range (~0.1–0.3 eV) characteristic of highly connected hydrogen-bond networks under nanoconfinement, enabling the near-continuous low-barrier pathway observed above T_break.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Underpins the high-temperature, fully-percolating interfacial film regime where the EIS resistance is collapsed; low activation energy is the signature of the facile interfacial transport that defines H4.
required_material_features: surface-bound water/hydroxyl groups forming an extended H-bond network
proton-transfer activation energy ≤ 0.3 eV
short proton-hopping distances along the interface
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: high-T continuous interfacial film with collapsed EIS semicircle

descriptors.descriptor_text: The host matrix must maintain sufficient segmental flexibility or retain an amorphous bound-water/plasticiser phase below 253 K to prevent the pore walls from becoming rigid glass, which would disrupt interfacial proton connectivity and fragment the cluster network.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Ensures the confined interface remains dynamically disordered enough for proton hopping even when the bulk-like water pool has frozen; a glassy-brittle interface would kill the low-T percolation network and eliminate the resolvable EIS semicircle entirely.
required_material_features: polymer/gel host with glass transition temperature below 240 K or intrinsic bound-water plasticization
retention of segmental motion or fast local dynamics in the confining matrix at sub-zero temperatures
amorphous or highly disordered interfacial layer that resists crystallization
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: low-T cluster percolation and EIS semicircle emergence (τ entering measurement window)

descriptors.descriptor_text: The confining host must provide a distribution of interconnected, hydrophilic surface sites (e.g., silanol, hydroxyl, carboxyl groups) that can anchor and orient the proton-conducting phase into a continuous thin film above a critical hydration/acid-loading threshold.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Creates the interfacial percolation backbone; without such anchoring sites, the liquid phase would be free to coalesce into droplets rather than wetting the pore walls as a contiguous film, preventing the multi-threshold network behavior of H4.
required_material_features: surface functional groups capable of hydrogen-bonding to water/acid
sufficient site density to maintain film connectivity
chemical stability of anchoring groups in acidic aqueous environment
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: interfacial film percolation threshold and high-T continuous pathway

descriptors.descriptor_text: The overall composite must exhibit a resolvable EIS semicircle at low temperature whose characteristic relaxation time shifts systematically with cooling, reflecting the growing resistance of the isolated cluster network as percolation connectivity is progressively lost.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Provides the diagnostic signature of H4: the emergence and evolution of a low-temperature arc that corresponds to the cluster-percolation resistance entering the measurement bandwidth.
required_material_features: measurable capacitive response at the cluster–cluster junctions
resistance increase with cooling such that the RC time constant falls within the accessible frequency range
no competing dielectric relaxations that obscure the cluster-network semicircle
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H4: EIS evolution from capacitive tail to resolved semicircle as T decreases

extraction_notes: Extracted 7 descriptors from H4 (confinement-induced multi-threshold percolation). D2 and D3 explicitly encode the cold-to-room-T operability window (182–299 K and sub-zero acid mobility) as mandated. D1 and D6 establish the confinement and surface functionalization backbone; D4 sets the interfacial hopping energy scale; D5 addresses matrix flexibility below 253 K; D7 captures the diagnostic EIS signature for experimental validation. All descriptors are framed as abstract functional requirements without naming specific material candidates.
